wikitext2_bigram_conditioning.description: WikiText-2 line-level language modelling with GPT-2 BPE tokens: held-out likelihood of a canonical token LM.
wikitext2_bigram_conditioning.notes: Scaled setting: the paper's GPT-2/Llama models are replaced by a first-order token (bigram) language model over a fixed 2048-token GPT-2 BPE support derived from the full training file; the held-out cohort is every test line whose tokens all lie in that support. The relative_log_loss_to_baseline results below are derived from the paper's GPT-2 small row of Figure 3 (local / baseline and global / baseline) as qualitative context; absolute bits/string are not comparable across model scales and are produced only in the score files. Paper GPT-2 small bits/string (baseline, local, global): 369.2, 367.0, 367.3.

relative_log_loss_to_baseline.description: Primary metric: exact held-out bits per string of the normalized submitted model divided by the bits per string of the evaluator-owned unconstrained baseline on the same strings; below 1.0 means a better held-out fit than the baseline.

log_loss_bits_per_string.description: Exact held-out negative log2-likelihood per string of the submitted model after the evaluator normalizes it over all finite token strings.

loss_improvement_bits_per_string.description: Evaluator-owned baseline bits per string minus the submitted model's bits per string on the same held-out strings.

log_loss_bits_per_token.description: Held-out bits divided by the evaluator's own token count, to catch gains concentrated on long or short strings.

canonical_sample_rate.description: Constraint (the paper's canonicality rate Z): exact probability that a string drawn from the submitted model is canonical, i.e. every adjacent token pair is canonical. It must be 1 (within 1e-9); otherwise the submission is scored at the failure floor (the uniform canonical model's loss).

The primary relative_log_loss_to_baseline values are derived from those rows to keep the scaled reproduction comparable without rescaling or fabricating absolute losses.
